decisions.difference: A: (Male genitalia finding)  vs  B: (or (Male genitalia finding) (Urethral discharge))
decisions.reason: The page treats urethral discharge as one of the man's "genital symptoms" (its first approach column), and Urethral discharge is not a descendant of Male genitalia finding, so without it a discharge-only man gets no check.

decisions.difference: A: complaint = (Male genitalia finding)  vs  B: complaint = (or (Male genitalia finding) (Urethral discharge))
decisions.reason: Same complaint as the trigger: "the man with genital symptoms" includes urethral discharge.

"Check for urethral discharge" is on the page, but with urethral discharge in the trigger a check_for of it is self-referential (Will's constraint, confirmed by page_check); the finding stays in the trigger and the urethritis rule.

decisions.difference: A: (Injury of scrotum), (Injury of testis)  vs  B: (Traumatic injury)
decisions.reason: The page says "preceding trauma" without a site, which B's Traumatic injury matches, but Injury of scrotum/testis are not its descendants in SNOMED, so a recorded scrotal injury would otherwise be missed.

decisions.difference: A: absent  vs  B: (Overexertion and strenuous movements) event
decisions.reason: The page names "strenuous activity" as a torsion criterion and this is the only exact SNOMED match; it passes the database check, though it is an event rather than a finding.

decisions.difference: A: absent  vs  B: (Testicle out of place)
decisions.reason: Page: "affected testicle higher"; no exact concept exists and Testicle out of place is the closest (broader) finding, better than leaving the criterion out.

decisions.difference: A: absent  vs  B: (Testes - transverse lie)
decisions.reason: Page: "rotated"; a transverse lie is the recorded finding of a rotated testicle, and leaving it out makes the rule fire less often than the page intends.

notes: Both builds passed; base is B, which encodes every torsion criterion the page lists and includes urethral discharge in the complaint. Rule descriptions are B's. Adding urethral discharge to check_for (A) was tried and rejected by page_check as SELF-REFERENTIAL check_for. All other conditions (paraphimosis, priapism >= 4 hours, urethritis, balanitis, possible testicular cancer, Urgent rule) were identical in both builds. Remaining questions are B's, plus A's torsion-pain question and the reconciler's questions on trauma site and the strenuous-activity event.
